pages.description: Nabila Habiby was given 28 months in jail after stealing her friend's £188,000 art collection.
pages.text: Art thief who targeted Edgar Davids is sentenced to jail Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Art thief jailed after targeting Edgar Davids 10 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Metropolitan Police A friend of ex-Premier League star Edgar Davids who stole his £188,000 modern art collection has been jailed in her absence for 28 months. Nabila Habiby, 39, sent multiple works of art belonging to Davids to auction, after he had trusted her to put his possessions into storage during a house move. Ther former Spurs midfielder believed the works were secured in a storage facility in Enfield, north London and only became suspicious when a luxury watch went missing. During sentencing on Wednesday at Wood Green Crown Court, Judge Alexander Jacobs said Habiby, who had failed to turn up for four previous court hearings, had a "streak of dishonesty throughout her relationships with others". He also said she "appears to be someone who thinks nothing of breaching the trust placed in her by people who consider them to be friends". A warrant has been issued for for her arrest and she is now expected to be brought back from Belgium to the UK to serve her sentence. The court heard Habiby, a former wealth manager, "abused her position as a friend to essentially steal". pages.title: Artemis IV - NASA
pages.description: NASA is targeting the first Artemis lunar landing in early 2028. After launching the crew aboard the Orion spacecraft, they will transfer to a commercial lunar lander for transport to the surface of the Moon. Lander readiness will determine which provider will safely carry them to the surface and back to Orion in lunar orbit before the crew returns home aboard Orion—splashing down safely in the Pacific Ocean.

These fossils were preserved within expanding and contracting wetlands between 100,000-12,500 years ago. Many of the Pleistocene animals of Tule Springs are still alive today, including the coyote ( Canis latrans ), jackrabbit ( Lepus sp.), and aquatic snails. Some animals went extinct, disappearing from North America entirely. Columbian mammoths belonged to the same family as living elephants.
